svg.text: Orbit-aware double large prime: why the phase coefficient matters
Koblitz curve, pi(x,y) = (x^2,y^2) acts on the order-r subgroup as [lambda]; log pi^k(Q) = lambda^k log Q, log(-Q) = -log Q. Status: implemented, measured on toy curves (RESULTS.md).
(ii) plain graph: vertices are points
row 1: S1 + Q = [a1]G + [b1]T
row 2: S2 + pi^3(Q) = [a2]G + [b2]T
Q
degree 1
pi^3(Q)
degree 1
two degree-one vertices: both rows peel, no relation
(they are conjugates, but the graph cannot see it)
(iii) orbit graph: vertices are signed Frobenius orbits
row 1: S1 + f1 * rep f1 = eps1 * lambda^(-k1)
row 2: S2 + f2 * rep f2 = eps2 * lambda^(-k2)
orbit(Q)
degree 2
row1 - (f1/f2) row2 : large column cancels
emits a small-only relation with sources {1, 2}
Curve replay (does not trust the filter or the table)
Check sum over small columns [v_c] Q_c == [rhs] G + [B] T with scalar multiplications only.
Right phase: both sides equal, row verified. Wrong phase, flipped sign or identifier-only merge: the filter still cancels the column
by arithmetic and the linear replay agrees, but the group identity fails (unit test, orbit.rs). Failures are counted, never filtered.
